quoted_sources.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. quoted_sources.reading: Expose Weakness is a TARGET-side debuff: 8% (melee) / 5% (ranged) increased damage FROM ALL SOURCES. Melee-first ordering of {{rd|a|b}} confirmed against Grasp ({{rd|3.5%|1.4%}} max-health damage) and Fleet Footwork ({{rd|10%|6%}} bonus AD).

quoted_sources.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
quoted_sources.reading: Carve is also a target-side debuff (armor REDUCTION, not penetration), so it lowers mitigation for every physical source in the roster, not only the holder.

quoted_sources.quote: R_final = max(0, (R - r_flat)*(1 - r_pct/100)*(1 - p) - f)
quoted_sources.reading: Reduction (Carve) composes before penetration; a Cleaver+lethality build drives post-pen resistance well below the target's nominal armor.
The pre-/post-mitigation ratio for a damage-linked heal is exactly 1 + R/100.

quoted_sources.reading: The dominant wiki convention for damage-linked heals is a POST-mitigation basis (same wording in the cached Aphelios Severum and Nilah passives quoted in data/champion-audit/batch-0.json and batch-4.json).

quoted_sources.where: docs/math-foundations.md section 5 audit table (Grievous Wounds row) and section 2.3 (Black Cleaver row)
quoted_sources.quote: Grievous Wounds ... multiplicative factor 0.60 (40% reduction); strongest-wins composition via min of factors | Black Cleaver average stacks ... the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp min(k, C) over h hits is C - C(C-1)/(2h) for h >= C
quoted_sources.reading: Neither candidate value is reachable from a GW factor (0.60) nor from a BC stack-model change: swapping the 0.8*max_stacks constant (24% reduction) for the exact Cesaro mean (27% at h=20) moves single-hit damage by ~1.7% at 100 armor, two orders of magnitude too small to explain a 26.7% move.

independent_computation.definition_used: overheal = max(0, heal_amount - (max_health - current_health)) at the heal's timestamp; it is a DERIVED leaf of the coupled health path, not a primitive wiki quantity.

step_1_direct_formula_search.goal: Test whether either value is itself a wiki-sourced heal amount (the case overheal == heal, i.e. healer at full health).
checks: Grasp of the Undying heal 1.3% (melee) / 0.52% (ranged) of max health: 71.5 would require 5,500 max health, 97.6 would require 7,508 - out of range for the corpus.
Sundered Sky 'heal you for {{rd|100%|50%}} base AD (+ 6% of your missing health)': overheal = baseAD - 0.94*missing, which pins neither value without the health path.
Literal grep of data/ for '97.6' and '71.5': only unrelated per-level damage arrays (Graves P per-level scaling 97.6 at level 17; Rell/Lillia/Bel'Veth-style arrays for 71.5) - no heal row.
step_1_direct_formula_search.result: No cached wiki formula produces 97.6 or 71.5 as a standalone heal amount. The leaf is therefore path-dependent.

step_2_delta_consistency_with_S1.model: Same heal amount, larger missing health in the new run: delta_overheal = extra post-mitigation damage the healed participant had absorbed by t_55.
step_2_delta_consistency_with_S1.reading: The observed delta is exactly what Bloodsong's Expose Weakness (S1: 8% melee / 5% ranged, 'increased damage from all sources') adds on 326-522 of accumulated damage against that participant - an ordinary per-participant damage total in a roster fight. A merge engine that finally applies a target-side amp to every source (allies, DoTs, item procs) rather than only to the holder's own hits reproduces this sign and magnitude, and S1's 'from all sources' is the wiki text that requires it.

step_3_ratio_consistency_with_S4_S5.model: Alternative reading: the heal itself is damage-linked and was re-based from pre-mitigation to post-mitigation.
step_3_ratio_consistency_with_S4_S5.reading: R = 36.5 is a realistic post-composition resistance for exactly this build: nominal armor ~100, Carve -30% (S2) -> 70, then percent pen + lethality (S3) -> mid-30s. Under S5 the post-mitigation basis is the wiki-correct one for damage-linked heals, so the smaller (new) value is the one on the sourced basis.

step_4_falsification_attempts: Grievous Wounds (0.60 factor, S6): 97.6 * 0.60 = 58.56 - does not yield 71.5. Rejected.
Melee/ranged mis-read of {{rd|8%|5%}} (S1): damage ratio 1.08/1.05 = 1.029 - two orders too small to be the whole delta. Rejected as the sole cause.
Additive vs multiplicative amp merge: (1+a)(1+b) / (1+a+b) with a,b <= 0.10 is <= 1.01 - cannot produce 1.365. Rejected as the sole cause.
Black Cleaver stack-model change (S6): ~1.7% single-hit damage move. Rejected as the sole cause.

Gnar Mega-form stat delta (branch-adjacent): Mini Gnar caches base AD 60 (+3.2) and base health 540 (+79) (data/champions.json); the level-18 growth factor is exactly 17, so no plausible Mega base-stat delta lands on 26.1, and the cached Rage Gene text ('Mega Gnar's gained health is not affected by healing modifiers'; 'retains his current health percentage') gives no 26.1 anchor. Rejected.
independent_computation.conclusion: Two independent consistency checks (delta = amp x accumulated damage under S1; ratio = 1 + R/100 at a build-plausible R under S3/S4/S5) both point to the LOWER value as the one produced by the wiki-correct rule, and every falsification attempt for the higher value failed. I could not reproduce either number exactly, because overheal at event index 55 is a function of the whole coupled health path, which is not reconstructible from data/ + docs/math-foundations.md alone.

limits_of_this_oracle: The scenario definition (roster, levels, builds, fight window) lives outside the permitted evidence tree, so the timeline could not be simulated.
healing_events[55] is a downstream leaf: it depends on every damage event that landed on the healed participant before t_55. No cached wiki text pins it.

Therefore the verdict is a rule-level and magnitude-level judgement, not an exact recomputation. If the parent has the sibling leaves (heal amount, target, timestamp, and the participant's max/current health at t_55), an exact check is possible: verify overheal == max(0, heal_amount - (max_health - current_health)) and that heal_amount uses the post-mitigation basis of S5.
No evidence was found that BOTH values are wrong; 'both_wrong' is not supported by anything in the cache.
